title: Triangulation
description: Introducing a third party into a dynamic to manufacture rivalry, jealousy, and insecurity.

sections.title: Quick Understanding
sections.content: Triangulation is the psychological architecture of a love triangle, weaponized. A manipulator will deliberately bring a third person—an ex, a coworker, a friend, or even a family member—into your relationship dynamic. By comparing you unfavorably to this third person, or by showing them excessive attention, the manipulator forces you to compete for their approval.

sections.title: Manipulator's Objective
content: Manufacture jealousy and severe insecurity.
Increase their own perceived value by creating artificial 'demand'.
Distract from their own abusive behaviors by creating a secondary conflict.
Divide and conquer. Prevent the victim and the third party from ever talking directly to compare notes.

sections.title: How The Tactic Works
content: Step 1: The manipulator establishes a connection with a third party.
Step 2: The manipulator casually mentions how amazing, successful, or attractive the third party is.
Step 3: The manipulator creates scenarios where the victim feels explicitly excluded or less-than.
Step 4: The victim panics, feels inadequate, and works twice as hard to 'win back' the manipulator's favor.

sections.title: Common Tactics Used
content: The Jealousy Trap: 'My ex used to love doing this with me. Why don't you?'
The Manufactured Flirtation: Openly flirting with waitstaff or friends right in front of you.
The Messenger Pigeon: Refusing to communicate with you directly, instead passing passive-aggressive messages through their mother or best friend.
The False Consensus: 'Even Sarah agrees with me that you are acting crazy.'

sections.title: Real Conversation Examples
content: Victim: 'It makes me uncomfortable how much you text your coworker at midnight.'
Manipulator: 'Oh my god, you are so insecure. She actually respects my career, unlike you. I guess I'll just tell her you're too jealous for me to have friends.'
Result: The victim is forced to drop the boundary to prove they aren't 'insecure', while the manipulator continues the boundary-violating behavior.

sections.title: Escalation Pattern
content: Early stage: Harmless-sounding praise of an ex or a coworker that leaves you vaguely uneasy.
Middle stage: Openly prioritizing the third party's feelings and needs over yours during conflicts.
Advanced stage: Maintaining full parallel relationships or affairs, and heavily blaming you for 'driving them into the arms of someone else' because of your flaws.

sections.title: Why Victims Fall For It
content: Core insecurities: Everyone has a primal fear of being replaced. The manipulator presses directly on this nerve.
The desire to 'win': It triggers a competitive instinct. If you can just prove you are better than the third party, you 'win' the prize (the manipulator).
Distraction: You become so focused on hating the third party that you forget to hold the manipulator accountable for their betrayal.

sections.title: Early Warning Signs
content: They talk about previous partners constantly, either placing them on a pedestal or demonizing them entirely.
Whenever you try to hold them accountable, they suddenly bring up what a third person 'thinks'.
You feel an intense, unnatural rivalry with someone you barely even know.

sections.title: Advanced Warning Signs
content: You spend hours cyberstalking their ex or coworker.
You feel completely replaceable. They have actively built a 'bench' of backup options.
They use your worst insecurities as the exact traits they 'admire' in the third person.

sections.title: Protection Strategies
content: Refuse to compete. The prize is a manipulator. Therefore, the winner actually loses. Opt out entirely.
Recognize the true enemy. The third party is usually either a fellow victim, or completely unaware of what is happening. The manipulator is the architect.
Establish absolute boundaries around respect. Comparison is an immediate dealbreaker.

sections.title: Counter-Moves
content: Fails: Trying to out-perform the third person. Snooping on the third person. Complaining about the third person. (You are feeding the manipulator exactly the drama they want).
Works: Non-participation. 'I am not going to compete for your respect. If they are a better fit for you, you should be with them.'
Works: Calling out the architecture. 'It is highly disrespectful that you keep comparing me to your ex. I will not tolerate being triangulated.'

sections.title: Reality Check
sections.content: A healthy partner shuts down external threats to the relationship instantly to protect you. A triangulating manipulator artificially creates threats to the relationship to control you.
